primitives.name: Posture Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: 4 N F L WAY T O P L AY POSTURE Proper posture at the start of a play before the ball is snapped is critical.
primitives.assumptions: Posture is a deterministic function of biomechanical alignment; stability and visibility are scalar metrics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P_0 fails to satisfy S > threshold and V > threshold, performance degrades.

layer2.mapping: Posture dynamics form the initial condition kernel for GSE state transitions; GSI infers deviation from normative posture via kinematic tracking.
layer2.telemetry: Kinematic alignment angles and ground reaction forces

primitives.name: Approach Behavior
primitives.verbatim_quote: APPROACH What happens between the ball being snapped and prior to contact is called the approach.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A': 'approach phase duration (seconds)', 'K': 'knee bend angle (degrees)', 'P': 'pad position indicator (unitless)', 'H': 'head orientation (degrees)'}
primitives.assumptions: Approach is a bounded temporal interval with fixed biomechanical constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when K < threshold, P < threshold, or H < threshold.

layer2.mapping: Approach behavior maps to GSE action space; GSI evaluates behavioral consistency using temporal windowed kinematic features.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal kinematic feature vectors and joint angle time-series

primitives.name: Contact Confidence
primitives.verbatim_quote: CONTACT Players need to be confident, capable and consistent throughout the contact phase of a play.
primitives.assumptions: Contact confidence is a composite of risk control and force execution metrics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When C < threshold or R > threshold, contact integrity is compromised.

layer2.mapping: Contact confidence defines terminal reward in GSE MDP; GSI models it as a probabilistic outcome of posture and approach.
layer2.telemetry: Force magnitude, directionality, and impact timing data

The three-way decomposition of posture, approach, and contact forms a sequential dynamical system where each phase is a state transition governed by biomechanical constraints. Posture sets the initial configuration, approach governs motion within a bounded temporal window, and contact determines final outcome. This structure enables a hierarchical Bayesian model in GSI where each phase contributes to a cumulative risk score. In GSE, this translates into a Markov decision process with discrete actions corresponding to posture adjustments, approach maneuvers, and contact protocols. Failure modes arise when any phase violates its prescribed constraints—e.g., improper knee bend during approach leads to instability in contact. The system exhibits duality between static posture and dynamic approach, with contact serving as the convergence point. Mathematical modeling treats these as stochastic processes with latent variables representing player intent and environmental noise.
